intent.raw: Run Research Tower on the local paper Monoidal Categories and Multicategories so the research can be executed, audited, and extended.
intent.objective: Plan and execute a governed notation-heavy research tower for Oliver Lugg's Monoidal Categories and Multicategories, producing source-first claims, notation bridge, glossary, definitions, distilled knowledge, equivalence proof spine, Arcanum bridge decisions, final learning pack, and explicit residue.
intent.operator_sentence: Use a notation-first Research Tower route to learn the Leinster-Hermida equivalence in source language first, then translate it into Arcanum-safe operator knowledge without promoting category-theory terms into canon.

route_menu.context_hint: The source is a notation-heavy 51-page category theory paper. The selected route is standard Research Tower execution with proof-spine closure, not full formalization.

items.label: Standard notation-heavy tower
items.description: Build a complete local research tower with notation bridge, claim ledger, glossary, definitions, distill, proof spine, bridge decision, and final learning pack.

items.label: Deep proof audit
items.description: Spawn role-bound proof and bibliography lanes to audit every omitted or diagram-heavy proof step.

items.label: Compact summary
items.description: Produce only a short source summary and glossary; faster but not enough to test Research Tower.

technique_overlays.trigger: The paper depends on formal notation for categories, multicategories, tensor products, coherence isomorphisms, representations, and the functor V.
technique_overlays.validation_expectation: The final learning pack must point to a notation bridge before using theorem-spine notation.

technique_overlays.trigger: The run creates glossary, definitions, and Arcanum bridge decisions that could be mistaken for canonical terms.
technique_overlays.validation_expectation: All outputs remain local research artifacts unless a separate governed promotion decision is opened.

steps.name: Recover local PDF source and source selectors
stop_conditions: Block if the PDF cannot be read or extracted.
Flag if extraction drops theorem-critical notation.

steps.name: Build Research Tower scaffold and closure plan
convergence_criteria: Tower names the source boundary, reading order, artifact roles, and local-only promotion scope.
Residue separates standard operator understanding from proof audit and formalization.
stop_conditions: Block if the tower claims canonical promotion authority.
Flag if closure gates are missing.

steps.name: Build notation bridge before synthesis
convergence_criteria: Paper-specific notation is explained before the theorem spine.
Reusable notation patterns are linked to the shared research notation glossary.
stop_conditions: Block if `C(A1 ... An; B)`, tensor notation, coherence notation, and `V(C)` are unexplained.

steps.name: Extract source claim ledger and equivalence proof spine
convergence_criteria: Every theorem-spine claim has source-kind labeling.
The proof route preserves construction direction: `UMonCat -> Multicat -> RMulticat` and back through representability.
stop_conditions: Block if the theorem is generalized from `RMulticat` to all `Multicat`.
Flag omitted diagram-heavy proof details as explicit residue.

steps.name: Build glossary, governed definitions, and distilled operator knowledge
convergence_criteria: Glossary terms preserve source meaning before Arcanum reading.
Definitions include formal shape, intuition, and misuse warning.
stop_conditions: Block canonical promotion of category-theory vocabulary.
Flag analogy-heavy entries without source meaning.

steps.name: Build Arcanum bridge decisions
convergence_criteria: Bridge decisions classify borrow-carefully, analogy-only, block, and promotion candidates.
No category-theory term is promoted into Arcanum canon.
stop_conditions: Block if `tensor`, `multicategory`, or `representability` are promoted as runtime terms.

steps.name: Synthesize final learning pack
convergence_criteria: Final pack begins from notation and source-first spine.
Final pack includes borrow, analogy-only, block, closed residue, and honest cutoff.
stop_conditions: Block if the final pack omits the notation entry point.
Block if the final pack claims proof-formalization closure.

steps.name: Validate route, artifacts, and residue
convergence_criteria: Dispatch validates against the Dispatch Spec validator.
Open residue has named next routes.
Research Tower test result records hardening lessons.
stop_conditions: Flag if residue lacks next route.

subagent_strategy.trigger: A deeper execution would need separate proof-audit, bibliography, notation, and Arcanum-bridge lanes.
subagent_strategy.explanation: The standard parent-lane run can close operator understanding, but full confidence in the proof details and bibliography comparison benefits from role-bound sibling agents with explicit closeout.
context: The current selected route is standard notation-heavy execution.
Deep proof audit and external-source verification remain open residue.

roles.purpose: Audit the theorem route, omitted diagram chases, and full/faithful/essentially-surjective claims.
Verify that theorem-critical notation is explained before synthesis.
Check Hermida, Leinster, and related cited works when a deep pass is authorized.
Preserve analogy-only boundaries and block accidental vocabulary promotion.

subagent_strategy.permission_prompt: Spawn proof, notation, bibliography, and Arcanum-bridge research lanes for a deeper Research Tower pass?

gates.condition: The local PDF is readable and theorem-critical sections can be extracted or cited by page/section.
NOTATION.md exists before final synthesis and explains category, multicategory, tensor, representation, and V notation.
Glossary, definitions, bridge, and final pack are local-research-only and do not promote category-theory terms into canonical Arcanum artifacts.
If deep subagents are spawned, every lane must have joined, closed, blocked with residue, or handed off before parent success.

boundaries.contract: Research outputs may recommend analogy or future work, but cannot promote Inventory, Ontology, glossary, sigil, spell, or runtime terms.

state_namespaces.write_policy: write local research artifacts only; no canonical promotion
append reusable research notation explanations only; no canonical glossary promotion

promotion_splits.rule: Research artifacts can list promotion candidates, but mutation of canonical targets requires a separate governed promotion decision.
